policy.description: Blocking line-coverage ratchets. Update measured counts in the same reviewed change whenever scope or coverage advances; never lower a floor without an explicit, justified scope change.

tolerance.rationale: Dismissible Smart Refresh notices add a state-watermarked dismissal latch, an additive active-server ShowNotices policy, accessible dual actions, and presentation-only suppression in core/live-update.ts. The legitimate core scope increase is 29 instrumented lines (2637→2666); compatibility, dismissal/retry/re-arm, live suppression, Ask-mode regressions, and download lifecycle regressions raise the reviewed high-water by 30 covered lines (2295→2325, 87.209%). Two clean Node 22.20/V8 full-suite coverage runs on 2026-07-25 each passed all 1524 tests across 223 files and reproduced exactly 2325/2666. Retaining the one-line tolerance makes the minimum 2324/2666 (87.172%), stricter than both the prior 2295/2637 high-water percentage (87.031%) and its 2294/2637 tolerated floor (86.993%). coverage-baseline.test.js retains the exact below-floor, above-baseline, scope-change, and broad-tolerance negative boundaries.

The server-owned download lifecycle feature adds bounded Sonarr/Radarr queue and history paging, deterministic O(q+h) reconciliation and normalization, stable persisted instance identity (including pre-edit legacy migration), user/library/Seerr authorization, fail-closed partial-source envelopes, bounded ARR response streaming, Manage-status normalization, configuration controls, and policy-aware recursive allowlisted Seerr download-status projection. Exact-episode privacy hardening additionally records sanitized episode-detail evidence so an inaccessible or malformed Sonarr episode can never inherit authorization from its parent Series. That correction adds 15 instrumented lines to the reviewed complete-assembly scope (30606→30621); queue/history, request-policy, administrator-minimization, and malformed-title regressions raise the high-water by 30 covered lines (22047→22077, 72.098%). Three clean .NET 10.0.9/Coverlet runs on 2026-07-25 each passed all 1942 tests and measured 22076, 22076, or 22077 covered lines out of 30621, establishing 22077 as the reviewed high-water. Retaining the evidence-bounded five-line Coverlet tolerance makes the minimum 22072/30621 (72.081%), stricter than both the prior 22042/30606 tolerated floor (72.019%) and the prior 22047/30606 high-water (72.035%). coverage-baseline.test.js retains the exact scope-drift, regression, stale-baseline, and broad-tolerance negative boundaries.
